x: First leg is generally quite a "tear-up" and Redwood had the task of getting us off to a good start. At all times he was dogging the leaders, and his was truly a great effort in gaining sixth place.

Redwood on stage three, firmly established himself in the "Hampshire" class by gaining five places with a superb 7-21 Jack himself recorded the same time on the next leg-taking us up two further places, and 7 minutes-41 secs later Morrison crossed the finishing line in fourth place to set the seal o…
Redwood took over and brought us to second with an excellent run of 10.45 (second fastest of the day). We were then only eleven seconds in arrears when Morrison took over for the last leg.
Winner Alan Morrison (4:37.2) was followed by Steer (4:39.0) 3rd, Bicourt (4:40.0)-and still a Youth,- 4th, and Redwood, Angus and Satchell making it 6 in 9.

In a Junior match Mitcham proved too strong for us but all praise to Cocks for his win in the 440 (50.6) and for grand supporting roles played by Redwood (4:35·7) Mead (55.8), Morrison (2:2.1) and Pottinger (19'11½") in their respective events.
